teams.heading: Ben Spencer undergoes shoulder surgery, putting his November Test availability in doubt
teams.body: Bath have confirmed that scrum-half Ben Spencer is a doubt for England's November Tests after undergoing shoulder surgery. The 34-year-old had the operation to resolve a long-standing issue following the summer tour. While his club expect him back later this autumn, the recovery timeline severely threatens his chances of facing Australia. With Spencer sidelined, Steve Borthwick faces a key selection dilemma, likely leaning on Alex Mitchell and Jack van Poortvliet as his primary options.

lead.why: The Bath scrum-half's post-tour shoulder surgery presents Steve Borthwick with a key selection puzzle ahead of the November internationals.

teams.heading: Jack Crowley ruled out of Ireland's November matches with vascular injury
teams.body: Ireland have suffered a major setback with news that fly-half Jack Crowley will remain sidelined until the new year. The 26-year-old Munster playmaker, who has won 35 caps, has been out since April with a lower limb vascular injury. Having already missed the July matches against Australia, Japan and New Zealand, Crowley is now ruled out of November's fixtures against Argentina, Fiji and South Africa. Munster head coach Clayton McMillan confirmed that "ensuring he gets back to 100% is the priority."

lead.why: Jack Crowley's extended injury absence ruling him out of the November internationals is the most significant news for the Irish national team.

teams.heading: Scottish Rugby braces for trial after High Court allows brain injury litigation
teams.body: Scottish Rugby is bracing for a landmark legal battle after the High Court ruled on Monday that the major brain injury lawsuit against the sport's governing bodies can proceed to trial. Hundreds of former players are suing over alleged negligence regarding concussion and long-term brain injuries. While the defendants had hoped to halt the litigation, the judge's decision to greenlight the trial leaves the future liability of the game in the balance, with no settlement or final judgment yet in sight.

lead.why: The High Court's ruling to proceed with the landmark brain injury lawsuit represents a massive, unresolved legal threat to Scottish Rugby.

teams.heading: Felipe Contepomi names unchanged Argentina starting side for Australia Test
teams.body: Head coach Felipe Contepomi has named an unchanged starting XV for Saturday's Test against Australia in Jujuy, rewarding the side that pushed South Africa close in their 17-10 defeat. Senior flanker Pablo Matera captains in the absence of Julián Montoya, who remains unavailable alongside Mateo Carreras, Santiago Chocobares and Marcos Kremer. The only alterations come on the bench, where Contepomi has reverted to a 5-3 split by naming prop Rodrigo Martinez and playmaker Nicolas Roger.

lead.why: Contepomi's decision to name an unchanged starting XV to face Australia is the day's most significant Argentina team news.

teams.heading: Les Kiss rests skipper Harry Wilson as Wallabies reshape for Argentina
teams.body: Wallabies coach Les Kiss has completely rotated his forward pack for Saturday's Test against Argentina in Salvador de Jujuy, resting regular captain Harry Wilson. Allan Alaalatoa takes over the captaincy, while Rob Valetini shifts to No. 8. Star recruit Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii returns from a minor hamstring strain but must settle for a place on the bench as Kiss seeks to build squad depth. "At the same time, we've selected a team that has lots of experience and proven combinations," Kiss said.

teams.heading: Timothy Lafaele and Japan internationals force league U-turn on eligibility rules
teams.body: Japan Rugby League One has settled a Tokyo District Court dispute by rolling back controversial restrictions on foreign-born players. The initial plan split domestic players into two categories, limiting matchday spots for naturalised citizens who lacked six years of Japanese schooling. Under the revised terms, players holding Japanese citizenship before May 2025 remain in the primary domestic category. Additionally, players with 30 or more caps for the Brave Blossoms will also receive reclassification to protect their livelihoods.

lead.why: Japan Rugby League One has backed down on controversial eligibility restrictions after players took legal action.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie complains to World Rugby regarding Springboks scrum before second Test
teams.body: New Zealand coach Dave Rennie has approached World Rugby regarding the officiating of the Springboks' scrum ahead of Saturday's second Test in Cape Town. Despite a victory at Ellis Park last weekend, the All Blacks’ front row of Ethan de Groot, Codie Taylor, and Tyrel Lomax was frequently under pressure during the opening half. Rennie is confident the dialogue will ensure a fairer contest at the set-piece, stating, “we think scrum-wise we will be a lot better.” The tourists also aim to sharpen their discipline following early penalties.

lead.why: Dave Rennie's formal complaint to World Rugby about scrum officiating is the most significant tactical and New Zealand-centric storyline ahead of today's Test.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus starts Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu as Handré Pollard misses New Zealand Test
teams.body: Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu returns to the starting XV for Saturday’s second Test in Cape Town after Handré Pollard was ruled out with a training-ground niggle. Pollard failed a fitness test on Friday, forcing Rassie Erasmus to pivot from a planned conservative approach. Despite the fly-half’s struggles in the 33-16 loss at Ellis Park, Rassie is backing the youngster’s adventurous skill set. Pollard has often delivered "under extreme pressure", but the Boks must now rely on Feinberg-Mngomezulu to reclaim the world No. 1 ranking.

lead.why: It covers a significant injury to the first-choice fly-half and a tactical selection shift for a major rivalry Test.
